name: hashrat
summary: Hashing tool supporting MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA512, Whirlpool, JH and their HMAC.
highlights: -list-hashes — Print a list of hashes that can be used with the '-type' option
-type — specify a hash type to use. This supports hashes coming from other subsystems, such as ope

flags.description: specify a hash type to use. This supports hashes coming from other subsystems, such as openssl. It also supports 'chaining' hash types like so: -type sha256,whirl

flags.name: -t
flags.description: Output hashes in traditional md5sum, shaXsum format

flags.name: -trad
flags.description: Output hashes in traditional md5sum, shaXsum format

flags.name: -bsd
flags.description: Output hashes in bsdsum format

flags.name: -tag
flags.description: Output hashes in bsdsum format

flags.name: --tag
flags.description: Output hashes in bsdsum format

flags.name: -r
flags.description: Recurse into directories when hashing files

flags.name: -hid
flags.description: Show hidden (starting with .) files

flags.name: -hidden
flags.description: Show hidden (starting with .) files

flags.name: -f
flags.description: Hash files listed in <listfile>

flags.name: -i
flags.description: Only hash items matching a comma-seperated list of shell patterns

flags.name: -x
flags.description: Exclude items matching a comma-sepearted list of shell patterns

flags.name: -X
flags.description: Exclude items matching shell patters stored in <file>

flags.name: -name
flags.description: <patterns> Only hash items matching a comma-seperated list of shell patterns (-name aka 'find')

flags.name: -mtime
flags.description: Only hash items <days> old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten days, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten days old

flags.name: -mmin
flags.description: <mins> Only hash items <min> minutes old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten mins, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten mins old

flags.name: -myear
flags.description: Only hash items <years> old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten years, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten years old

flags.name: -exec
flags.description: In CHECK or MATCH mode only examine executable files.

flags.name: -dups
flags.description: Search for duplicate files.

flags.name: -rename
flags.description: Rename files to <name>-<hash>.<extn>.

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Truncate hashes to <length> bytes

flags.name: -c
flags.description: CHECK hashes against list from file (or stdin)

flags.name: -cf
flags.description: CHECK hashes against list but only show failures

flags.name: -C
flags.description: Recursively CHECK directory against list of files on stdin

flags.name: -Cf
flags.description: Recursively CHECK directory against list but only show failures

flags.name: -m
flags.description: MATCH files from a list read from stdin.

flags.name: -lm
flags.description: Read hashes from stdin, upload them to a memcached server (requires the -memcached option).

flags.name: -mcd
flags.description: Specify memcached server. (Overrides reading list from stdin if used with -m, -c or -cf).

flags.name: -h
flags.description: Script to run when a file fails CHECK mode, or is found in MATCH mode.

flags.name: -hook
flags.description: Script to run when a file fails CHECK mode, or is found in FIND mode

flags.name: -color
flags.description: Use ANSI color codes on output when checking hashes.

flags.name: -strict
flags.description: Strict mode: when checking, check file mtime, owner, group, and inode as well as its hash

flags.name: -S
flags.description: Strict mode: when checking, check file mtime, owner, group, and inode as well as its hash

flags.name: -d
flags.description: dereference (follow) symlinks

flags.name: -fs
flags.description: Stay on one file system

flags.name: -dir
flags.description: DirMode: Read all files in directory and create one hash for them!

flags.name: -dirmode
flags.description: DirMode: Read all files in directory and create one hash for them!

flags.name: -devmode
flags.description: DevMode: read from a file EVEN IF IT'S A DEVNODE

flags.name: -lines
flags.description: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly.

flags.name: -rawlines
flags.description: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly, INCLUDING any trailing whitespace. (This is compatible with 'echo text | md5sum')

flags.name: -rl
flags.description: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly, INCLUDING any trailing whitespace. (This is compatible with 'echo text | md5sum')

flags.name: -cgi
flags.description: Run in HTTP CGI mode

flags.name: -xdialog
flags.description: Run in 'xdialog' (zenity, yad or qarama) mode

flags.name: -net
flags.description: Treat 'file' arguments as either ssh or http URLs, and pull files over the network and then hash them (Allows hashing of files on remote machines). URLs are in the format ssh://[username]:[password]@[host]:[port] or http://[username]:[password]@[host]:[port]..

flags.name: -idfile
flags.description: Path to an ssh private key file to use to authenticate INSTEAD OF A PASSWORD when pulling files via ssh.

flags.name: -xattr
flags.description: Use eXtended file ATTRibutes. In hash mode, store hashes in the file attributes, in check mode compare against hashes stored in file attributes.

flags.name: -txattr
flags.description: Use TRUSTED eXtended file ATTRibutes. In hash mode, store hashes in 'trusted' file attributes. 'trusted' attributes can only be read and written by root. Under freebsd this menas SYSTEM attributes.

flags.name: -attrs
flags.description: comma-separated list of filesystem attribute names to be set to the value of the hash.

flags.name: -cache
flags.description: Use hashes stored in 'user' xattr if they're younger than the mtime of the file. This speeds up outputting hashes. Also do not update xattr of a file if it already matches.

flags.name: -u
flags.description: Update. In checking mode, update hashes for the files as you go. <types> is a comma-separated list of things to update, which can be 'xattr' 'memcached' or a file name. This will update these targets with the hash that was found at the time of checking.

flags.name: -hide-input
flags.description: When reading data from stdin in linemode, set the terminal to not echo characters, thus hiding typed input.

flags.name: -star-input
flags.description: When reading data from stdin in linemode replace characters with stars.

flags.name: -xsel
flags.description: Update X11 clipboard and primary selections to the current hash. This works using Xterm command sequences. The xterm resource 'allowWindowOps' must be set to 'true' for this to work.

flags.name: -clip
flags.description: Update X11 clipboard to the current hash. This works using the 'xsel', 'xclip' or 'pbcopy' commands, or if none of those are installed falls back to Xterm clipboard as in the '-xsel' option .

flags.name: -qr
flags.description: Display the current hash as a qrcode. This requires the 'qrencode' command to be installed, and also an image viewer like fim, feh, or imagemagick display to be installed.

flags.name: -qrcode
flags.description: Display the current hash as a qrcode. This requires the 'qrencode' command to be installed, and also an image viewer like fim, feh, or imagemagick display to be installed.
